Please provide a comparative analysis of the following two research paper abstracts on the topic of lithium-ion battery degradation. 

Abstract A: 'This study investigates the impact of high-rate charging on the cycle life of NMC-graphite pouch cells. We employed electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and post-mortem analysis using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Our findings indicate that charging at rates above 2C leads to significant lithium plating on the anode surface, which is the primary driver for accelerated capacity fade. We propose a multi-stage charging protocol that mitigates this effect, extending cycle life by 30% compared to a standard constant-current constant-voltage (CCCV) method.'

Abstract B: 'We explore the role of solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer instability as a key degradation mechanism in silicon-graphite composite anodes. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), we observed that the SEI layer undergoes continuous dissolution and reformation during cycling, consuming active lithium and increasing cell impedance. Our results suggest that electrolyte additives, specifically fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), can stabilize the SEI layer, leading to a 50% improvement in capacity retention over 500 cycles.'

Your analysis should be structured to compare the following points for both abstracts: 1. Primary degradation mechanism identified. 2. Key experimental techniques used. 3.
